protocol.alignment_note: Provided phone timings; upstream does not document their construction or human verification. Treat as approximate labels.
protocol.source_files: All five train parquet shards; our own speaker-disjoint 60/20/20 training/validation/test split
protocol.selection: At most 20 tokens per phone per speaker, hash order, unique source word per phone/speaker; duration 160–400 ms, exact central 160 ms input, no tone/length marks in category labels
protocol.projection: Compare standardization + PCA96 + shrinkage LDA2 with direct class-balanced Ridge prediction of two fixed target coordinates. Choose encoder/method/alpha by validation nearest-centroid balanced accuracy. Persist selection, refit on development, evaluate final test once. Separate-map LDA validation is retained as a comparison only.
protocol.coordinates: Rotate/reflect using development class means and divide each coordinate by a common scale. No online refitting or speaker-dependent coordinate rotation. Native ellipses use development samples only.
protocol.latency: Rolling 160 ms audio window, 80 ms hop; one local inference request in flight, discard stale windows; animation interpolates results without pretending to increase measurement rate
protocol.evaluation: Final test balanced accuracy in 2D, per-class recall, 95% bootstrap interval by speaker, and +/-20 ms crop shift. Publish overlap honestly. Binary English results do not validate these Mandarin maps.
protocol.shared_map_amendment: User clarified one shared map after feature extraction and initial separate-map validation, before any final-test evaluation. Shared ASR LDA validation was 51.4%; validation exploration of direct coordinate regression was stronger. Final selection compares all three encoders with LDA or class-balanced Ridge (alpha 10, 100, 1000) after training-only standardization and PCA96. Only the shared map is deployed and final-tested. Validation was used for method development; it is not an unbiased performance estimate.

shared_targets.coordinates: Unit circle, angle=2*pi*index/9. These fixed layout targets are arbitrary display positions, not anatomical coordinates. Ridge predicts continuous coordinates directly; no softmax, snapping or forced category choice.
